notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) direct HTTP (requests and curl_cffi impersonate=chrome120) both hit a Cloudflare JS challenge ('Just a moment...', 403) on countryroad.com.au - robots.txt has no anthropic/Claude-specific disallow (User-agent: * / Allow: /), so tier (b) Playwright (headless chromium, sync API) was used and passed the challenge cleanly; all research done via Playwright page loads, no Chrome tab (tier c) needed. TREE: scope limited strictly to the 'Home' department (categoryId 5712, root url /home/) reached via the /home-new-in/ landing page; apparel/fashion/kids-clothing/etc departments were not traversed at all (out of scope). Full category tree was pulled from the Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ RTK-query cache embedded in each page's SSR HTML (crgApi.queries -> getProductListInitialData -> data.CategoryNavigation, a complete nested nav tree with categoryId per node), cross-checked against the site's own /sitemap/ footer page. This is more complete/reliable than the rendered DOM mega-menu, which is empty in the initial HTML and only populates on hover via client JS. QTY: exact totalCount taken from the same SSR-embedded cache (crgApi.queries -> getProductLanding-<categoryId> -> data.ProductLanding.totalCount), which is the backend's own authoritative product-list total (not a DOM-scraped 'N products' string). Every recorded leaf was verified by loading its own URL and confirming pageProps.canonicalPath / routeParams.categoryId matched the requested node before recording qty (a rendered <h1> regex proved unreliable - it sometimes grabbed text from an unrelated merchandising widget, e.g. it returned 'King Single Quilt Covers' on the Double Quilt Covers page - so canonical-path + categoryId match was used as the authoritative confirmation instead of h1 text). EXCLUDED: New In, NEW BRANDS (+ 6 brand sub-pages: Le Creuset/Conscious Loom/Marimekko/Lexon/Orbitkey/Kelly & Windsor), Our Edits, Our Editorials, Seasonal Events/Boxed Gifts - all promotional/brand/editorial landing pages, not genuine product-type categories, excluded per View-All/Collections rule. Kitchen & Dining's Cutlery/Dining/Glasses/Kitchen Accessories/Mugs/Drink Bottles & Reusable Cups/Serving/Cookware/Bakeware, Home Accessories' Candles & Holders/Decorator/Frames/Lighting/Furniture & Lighting/Vases/Audio & Tech, Outdoor/Picnic (1 item, a bowl), Pet section (Collars & Leads, Pet Accessories), Scent section (candles, home fragrance) - all excluded as non-textile/non-storage per category rules (checked several by sampling actual product titles, e.g. Decorator = mirrors/trinket boxes/clocks, Picnic = a single serving bowl, Kitchen Accessories = oil pourers/coasters/drink bottles with one stray apron buried in 136 mixed items with no way to isolate just the apron count). Bathroom Accessories (26 items) sampled and found to be a mixed bucket of bath robes + non-textile items (soap dishes, trays, toothbrush holders) with no clean split possible and no distinct storage function either - excluded entirely from both arrays (the dedicated Bath Robes node already captures the robes cleanly). Rugs' unlabeled node at /home-rugs-/ (totalCount 115, exactly = Indoor Rugs 85 + Outdoor Rugs 30) is the parent/all-rugs aggregate - dropped per the parent-URL rule since valid Indoor/Outdoor subcategories exist. Cushions and Throws each appear twice in the nav (once cross-linked under Bedroom, once under Home Accessories) but resolve to the identical URL/categoryId in both places - recorded once each, grouped under Home Accessories (their URL's actual namespace) to avoid duplicate rows. Two rows carry review flags: Table Linen & Accessories (Kitchen & Dining) mixes genuine table textiles (napkins, tablecloths, placemats) with non-textile accessories (coasters, napkin rings) under one URL with no facet-level split available - kept as Textile at LOW confidence per the site's own category name/hierarchy rather than dropped. Home Accessories > Storage (4 items: 2x Marble Jewellery Tray, Marble Ring Stand, Marble Round Storage) is explicitly named/hierarchied as a Storage category by the site but the individual products read as decorative marble trays/stands bordering the storage.md Section 23 decorative-vs-storage exclusion list - kept as Storage at LOW confidence rather than dropped, per the explicit website hierarchy naming.
